subject: botany
question_text: List the changes observed in an angiosperm flower subsequent to pollination and fertilization.

verification.note: Chapter 6 is sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany guide (book p.15), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO year citations. Only ONE source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely pending. The 2+2 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book prints 'chala-zogamy' (a scan hyphenation of chalazogamy) and 'pollen tube enters into ovules'; the card writes chalazogamy and 'enters the ovule'.

insider_note: Split the answer under the two headings exactly as asked — a mixed list makes the marker search for each point and usually costs one of the four marks.

steps.label: After pollination
lines: The pollen grain germinates on the stigma
The generative cell divides and forms two
The pollen tube grows through the stigma
and style and reaches the ovary.
It enters the ovule by porogamy,
steps.why: Pollination only lands the pollen on the stigma; every change that follows — tube, two male gametes, growth down the style, entry into the ovule — happens before fertilization and belongs in this half.
common_mistakes: Writing that the pollen grain travels down the style — the pollen TUBE grows down; the grain stays on the stigma.
Writing 'vegetative cell divides' — the GENERATIVE cell divides into the two male gametes.
steps.memory_tip: Entry routes by position: porogamy through the micropyle (the pore), mesogamy through the integuments (the middle), chalazogamy through the chalaza.
steps.margin_note: Four short points — tube, two male gametes, path, entry route.

lines: Sepals, petals and stamens wither and

lines.text: Zygote → embryo · ovary → fruit · ovule → seed

lines: develops into the endosperm, and the
steps.why: After fertilization every remaining part converts into a seed-and-fruit structure — zygote to embryo, ovary to fruit, ovule to seed, PEN to endosperm — while the display parts wither and fall.
common_mistakes: Swapping the pair — the OVARY becomes the fruit; each OVULE becomes a seed.
Writing that the endosperm comes from the zygote — it comes from the PEN (the triple-fusion product).
steps.memory_tip: Three conversions from small to large: zygote → embryo, ovule → seed, ovary → fruit.
steps.margin_note: The boxed conversion line is what the examiner scans for.
